title: Git Viewer
description: A standalone desktop app that scans a folder tree for git repositories and gives you a VSCode-style Source Control panel — status, staged and unstaged diffs, commit, fetch, pull, push and branch switching — without running an editor.
problem: I was tired of depending on each text editor's own implementation of git. I like the way VSCode handles it, but I don't want to run a full, bloated editor just to manage my repositories — especially now that they are all piling on agentic features with no real way to make them disappear.
approach: Tauri with a Rust core for the git operations and filesystem scanning, and a React + shadcn/ui front end for the interface. Diffs are rendered with the Monaco diff editor, so the part everyone actually looks at behaves exactly like the editor it is replacing.
